$$
\{\begin{aligned}x-y=2 \\ 2x+y=1.\end{aligned}
$$

 
According to Cramer's rule, the unknown $x$ can be written as
![](images/f5/f5c9b1c83ed648b56b47bd370ba5b15359521492087eda769d4122be99384a0f.svg)
Express $D_x$ in terms of a $2 \times 2$ determinant." :question/worked-solution "We are given the system

$$
\{\begin{aligned}x-y=2 \\ 2x+y=1.\end{aligned}
$$

 

The determinant of the coefficient matrix is

$$
\begin{aligned}D & =|\begin{aligned}1 & -1 \\ 2 & 1\end{aligned}|.\end{aligned}
$$

Now, to construct $D_x$, we replace the first column of the coefficient matrix by the right-hand side column of the given system:

$$
\begin{aligned}{D}_{x} & =|\begin{aligned}2 & -1 \\ 1 & 1\end{aligned}|\end{aligned}
$$" :db/ensure [:question/validate]} {:db/id 17592186119788 :knowledge-point/questions ["question-659100c2-e69a-5015-bd46-ea6499418f4e"] :db/ensure [:knowledge-point/validate]} {:db/id 17592186119599 :question/problem "Consider the system of equations 

$$
\{\begin{aligned}5x+2y=-1 \\ -3x+3y=9.\end{aligned}
$$

Express $y$ in terms of $2 \times 2$ determinants." :question/worked-solution "We are given the system

$$
\{\begin{aligned}5x+2y=-1 \\ -3x+3y=9.\end{aligned}
$$

The determinant of the coefficient matrix is

$$
\begin{aligned}D & =|\begin{aligned}5 & 2 \\ -3 & 3\end{aligned}|.\end{aligned}
$$

Now, to construct $D_y$, we replace the second column of the coefficient matrix by the right-hand side column of the given system:

$$
\begin{aligned}{D}_{y} & =|\begin{aligned}5 & -1 \\ -3 & 9\end{aligned}|\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, according to Cramer's rule, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}y & =\frac{{D}_{y}}{D}=\frac{|\begin{aligned}5 & -1 \\ -3 & 9\end{aligned}|}{|\begin{aligned}5 & 2 \\ -3 & 3\end{aligned}|}.\end{aligned}
$$" :db/ensure [:question/validate]} {:db/id 17592186119790 :knowledge-point/questions ["question-1485a2c5-d3d5-5ae7-bfda-a8f34f74aef0" "question-9a324339-2131-569e-b62b-73969b420199"] :db/ensure [:knowledge-point/validate]} {:db/id 17592186119601 :question/problem "Let $\langle x,3 \rangle$ be the solution of the system of equations below.

According to Cramer's rule, $x=$" :question/worked-solution "We are given the system

\{\begin{aligned}4x+6y=32 \\ 3x+5y=26.\end{aligned}
$$

The determinant of the coefficient matrix is

$$
\begin{aligned}D & =|\begin{aligned}4 & 6 \\ 3 & 5\end{aligned}|.\end{aligned}
$$

Now, we construct ${D}_{x}$, we replace the first column of the coefficient matrix by the right-hand side column of the given system:

$$
\begin{aligned}{D}_{x} & =|\begin{aligned}32 & 6 \\ 26 & 5\end{aligned}|.\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, according to Cramer's rule, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}x & =\frac{{D}_{x}}{D}=\frac{|\begin{aligned}32 & 6 \\ 26 & 5\end{aligned}|}{|\begin{aligned}4 & 6 \\ 3 & 5\end{aligned}|}.\end{aligned}
$$" :db/ensure [:question/validate]} {:db/id 17592186388632 :question/problem "Consider the system of equations 

$$
\{\begin{aligned}2x+8y=-14 \\ 5x+4y=13.\end{aligned}
$$

According to Cramer's rule, $y=$" :question/worked-solution "We are given the system

$$
\{\begin{aligned}2x+8y=-14 \\ 5x+4y=13.\end{aligned}
$$

The determinant of the coefficient matrix is

$$
\begin{aligned}D & =|\begin{aligned}2 & 8 \\ 5 & 4\end{aligned}|.\end{aligned}
$$

Now, to construct ${D}_{y}$ we replace the second column of the coefficient matrix by the right-hand side column of the given system:

$$
\begin{aligned}{D}_{y} & =|\begin{aligned}2 & -14 \\ 5 & 13\end{aligned}|.\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, according to Cramer's rule, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}y & =\frac{{D}_{y}}{D}=\frac{|\begin{aligned}2 & -14 \\ 5 & 13\end{aligned}|}{|\begin{aligned}2 & 8 \\ 5 & 4\end{aligned}|}.\end{aligned}
$$" :db/ensure [:question/validate]} {:db/id 17592186329702 :question/problem "Let $⟨-1,y⟩$ be the solution of the system of equations below. 

$$
\{\begin{aligned}3x+5y=k \\ 2x-y=-4.\end{aligned}
$$

Which of the following equations could be solved to find the value of $k?$

I. $|\begin{aligned}k & 5 \\ -4 & -1\end{aligned}|=-13$

II. $|\begin{aligned}k & 5 \\ -4 & -1\end{aligned}|=-1$

III. $|\begin{aligned}k & 5 \\ -4 & -1\end{aligned}|=13$" :db/ensure [:question/validate]} {:db/id 17592186271990 :question/problem "Let $⟨x,3⟩$ be the solution of the system of equations below. 

$$
\{\begin{aligned}kx+3y=1 \\ 7x-2y=8.\end{aligned}
$$

Which of the following equations could be solved to find the value of $k?$

I. $-3|\begin{aligned}k & 3 \\ 7 & -2\end{aligned}|=|\begin{aligned}k & 1 \\ 7 & 8\end{aligned}|$

II. $3|\begin{aligned}k & 3 \\ 7 & -2\end{aligned}|=|\begin{aligned}k & 1 \\ 7 & 8\end{aligned}|$

III. $|\begin{aligned}k & 3 \\ 7 & -2\end{aligned}|=3|\begin{aligned}k & 1 \\ 7 & 8\end{aligned}|$" :db/ensure [:question/validate]} {:db/id 17592186120448 :question/problem "Let $⟨x,3⟩$ be the solution of the system of equations below. 

$$
\{\begin{aligned}2x+3y=10 \\ kx-4y=12.\end{aligned}
$$

Which of the following equations could be solved to find the value of $k?$

I. $3|\begin{aligned}2 & 3 \\ k & -4\end{aligned}|=|\begin{aligned}2 & 10 \\ k & 12\end{aligned}|$

II. $|\begin{aligned}2 & 3 \\ k & -4\end{aligned}|=|\begin{aligned}2 & 10 \\ k & 12\end{aligned}|$

III. $|\begin{aligned}2 & 3 \\ k & -4\end{aligned}|=3|\begin{aligned}2 & 10 \\ k & 12\end{aligned}|$" :question/worked-solution "The determinant of the coefficient matrix is

$$
\begin{aligned}D & =|\begin{aligned}2 & 3 \\ k & -4\end{aligned}|.\end{aligned}
$$

According to Cramer's rule, the value of $y$ is given by $y=\frac{{D}_{y}}{D},$ where

$$
\begin{aligned}{D}_{y} & =|\begin{aligned}2 & 10 \\ k & 12\end{aligned}|.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore:

$$
\begin{aligned}y & =\frac{{D}_{y}}{D} \\ 3 & =\frac{|\begin{aligned}2 & 10 \\ k & 12\end{aligned}|}{|\begin{aligned}2 & 3 \\ k & -4\end{aligned}|} \\ 3|\begin{aligned}2 & 3 \\ k & -4\end{aligned}| & =|\begin{aligned}2 & 10 \\ k & 12\end{aligned}|\end{aligned}
$$

So, the correct answer is "I only"." :question/difficulty :question.difficulty/hard :db/ensure [:question/validate]} {:db/id 17592186118802 :answer-field/correct 17592186118805 :db/ensure [:answer-field/validate]} {:db/id "question-1485a2c5-d3d5-5ae7-bfda-a8f34f74aef0" :question/id #uuid "1485a2c5-d3d5-5ae7-bfda-a8f34f74aef0" :question/math-academy-id "q-77402" :question/problem "Let $⟨2,y⟩$ be the solution of the system of equations below. 

$$
\{\begin{aligned}4x+ky=5 \\ x+2y=-4\end{aligned}
$$

Which of the following equations could be solved to find the value of $k?$

I. $|\begin{aligned}4 & k \\ 1 & 2\end{aligned}|=|\begin{aligned}5 & k \\ -4 & 2\end{aligned}|$

II. $2|\begin{aligned}4 & k \\ 1 & 2\end{aligned}|=|\begin{aligned}5 & k \\ -4 & 2\end{aligned}|$

III. $|\begin{aligned}4 & k \\ 1 & 2\end{aligned}|=2|\begin{aligned}5 & k \\ -4 & 2\end{aligned}|$" :question/worked-solution "The determinant of the coefficient matrix is

$$
\begin{aligned}D & =|\begin{aligned}4 & k \\ 1 & 2\end{aligned}|.\end{aligned}
$$

According to Cramer's rule, the value of $x$ is given by $x=\frac{{D}_{x}}{D},$ where

$$
\begin{aligned}{D}_{x} & =|\begin{aligned}5 & k \\ -4 & 2\end{aligned}|.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore:

$$
\begin{aligned}x & =\frac{{D}_{x}}{D} \\ 2 & =\frac{|\begin{aligned}5 & k \\ -4 & 2\end{aligned}|}{|\begin{aligned}4 & k \\ 1 & 2\end{aligned}|} \\ 2|\begin{aligned}4 & k \\ 1 & 2\end{aligned}| & =|\begin{aligned}5 & k \\ -4 & 2\end{aligned}|\end{aligned}
$$

So, the correct answer is "II only"." :question/difficulty :question.difficulty/hard :question/answer-fields ["answer-field-1aec48af-7f8c-53fd-bb3d-101ace543e43"] :db/ensure [:question/validate]} {:db/id "answer-field-1aec48af-7f8c-53fd-bb3d-101ace543e43" :answer-field/id #uuid "1aec48af-7f8c-53fd-bb3d-101ace543e43" :answer-field/key "selection" :answer-field/type :answer-field.type/radio :answer-field/correct "answer-37e0bd1c-a3ae-5f52-a82d-3a71181d02f2" :answer-field/choices ["answer-13abba68-c603-520c-b95e-bae74246f467" "answer-ed90928a-c1d1-55de-ac12-d5f61d39fd02" "answer-8d3a2a97-810a-5f83-ae72-fc21a76e36d4" "answer-37e0bd1c-a3ae-5f52-a82d-3a71181d02f2" "answer-45f349a4-8a10-5b19-b4f8-85a49af13560"] :db/ensure [:answer-field/validate]} {:db/id "answer-13abba68-c603-520c-b95e-bae74246f467" :answer/id #uuid "13abba68-c603-520c-b95e-bae74246f467" :answer/type :answer.type/text :answer/value "I and II only" :db/ensure [:answer/validate]} {:db/id "answer-ed90928a-c1d1-55de-ac12-d5f61d39fd02" :answer/id #uuid "ed90928a-c1d1-55de-ac12-d5f61d39fd02" :answer/type :answer.type/text :answer/value "I only" :db/ensure [:answer/validate]} {:db/id "answer-8d3a2a97-810a-5f83-ae72-fc21a76e36d4" :answer/id #uuid "8d3a2a97-810a-5f83-ae72-fc21a76e36d4" :answer/type :answer.type/text :answer/value "II and III only" :db/ensure [:answer/validate]} {:db/id "answer-37e0bd1c-a3ae-5f52-a82d-3a71181d02f2" :answer/id #uuid "37e0bd1c-a3ae-5f52-a82d-3a71181d02f2" :answer/type :answer.type/text :answer/value "II only" :db/ensure [:answer/validate]} {:db/id "answer-45f349a4-8a10-5b19-b4f8-85a49af13560" :answer/id #uuid "45f349a4-8a10-5b19-b4f8-85a49af13560" :answer/type :answer.type/text :answer/value "III only" :db/ensure [:answer/validate]} {:db/id "question-9a324339-2131-569e-b62b-73969b420199" :question/id #uuid "9a324339-2131-569e-b62b-73969b420199" :question/math-academy-id "q-42985" :question/problem "Let $⟨-12,y⟩$ be the solution of the system of equations below. 

$$
\{\begin{aligned}7x+9y=42 \\ kx+10y=-4.\end{aligned}
$$

Which of the following equations could be solved to find the value of $k?$

I. $|\begin{aligned}7 & 9 \\ k & 10\end{aligned}|=-12$

II. $|\begin{aligned}7 & 9 \\ k & 10\end{aligned}|=-38$

III. $|\begin{aligned}7 & 9 \\ k & 10\end{aligned}|=456$" :question/worked-solution "The determinant of the coefficient matrix is

$$
\begin{aligned}D & =|\begin{aligned}7 & 9 \\ k & 10\end{aligned}|.\end{aligned}
$$

According to Cramer's rule, the value of $x$ is given by $x=\frac{{D}_{x}}{D},$ where

$$
\begin{aligned}{D}_{x} & =|\begin{aligned}42 & 9 \\ -4 & 10\end{aligned}| \\  & =420+36 \\  & =456.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore:

$$
\begin{aligned}x & =\frac{{D}_{x}}{D} \\ -12 & =\frac{456}{|\begin{aligned}7 & 9 \\ k & 10\end{aligned}|} \\ |\begin{aligned}7 & 9 \\ k & 10\end{aligned}| & =\frac{456}{-12} \\ |\begin{aligned}7 & 9 \\ k & 10\end{aligned}| & =-38\end{aligned}
$$

So, the correct answer is "II only"." :question/difficulty :question.difficulty/hard :question/answer-fields ["answer-field-cb7f776c-eb99-528b-aabd-b4033c71b940"] :db/ensure [:question/validate]} {:db/id "answer-field-cb7f776c-eb99-528b-aabd-b4033c71b940" :answer-field/id #uuid "cb7f776c-eb99-528b-aabd-b4033c71b940" :answer-field/key "selection" :answer-field/type :answer-field.type/radio :answer-field/correct "answer-bd29ef89-365b-598b-abba-79648038c1f5" :answer-field/choices ["answer-3cc8305b-aa26-5938-bd09-82bace4ba090" "answer-1f13ed83-8c4f-597b-9f02-b31307021e5b" "answer-f4490cc5-d61d-513b-835c-43fda69e74cc" "answer-bd29ef89-365b-598b-abba-79648038c1f5" "answer-742473cb-daf1-51d3-8173-d6d820c2cd4a"] :db/ensure [:answer-field/validate]} {:db/id "answer-3cc8305b-aa26-5938-bd09-82bace4ba090" :answer/id #uuid "3cc8305b-aa26-5938-bd09-82bace4ba090" :answer/type :answer.type/text :answer/value "I and II only" :db/ensure [:answer/validate]} {:db/id "answer-1f13ed83-8c4f-597b-9f02-b31307021e5b" :answer/id #uuid "1f13ed83-8c4f-597b-9f02-b31307021e5b" :answer/type :answer.type/text :answer/value "I only" :db/ensure [:answer/validate]} {:db/id "answer-f4490cc5-d61d-513b-835c-43fda69e74cc" :answer/id #uuid "f4490cc5-d61d-513b-835c-43fda69e74cc" :answer/type :answer.type/text :answer/value "II and III only" :db/ensure [:answer/validate]} {:db/id "answer-bd29ef89-365b-598b-abba-79648038c1f5" :answer/id #uuid "bd29ef89-365b-598b-abba-79648038c1f5" :answer/type :answer.type/text :answer/value "II only" :db/ensure [:answer/validate]} {:db/id "answer-742473cb-daf1-51d3-8173-d6d820c2cd4a" :answer/id #uuid "742473cb-daf1-51d3-8173-d6d820c2cd4a" :answer/type :answer.type/text :answer/value "III only" :db/ensure [:answer/validate]} {:db/id 17592186121027 :tutorial/content "**Cramer's Rule** is a method for solving a linear system of equations using determinants.

Suppose we have a square system of linear equations

$$
\{\begin{aligned}{a}_{11}x+{a}_{12}y={b}_{1} \\ {a}_{21}x+{a}_{22}y={b}_{2},\end{aligned}
$$

where ![](images/c7/c7ef883a1d4dd8c1fc0fc8fbde5ed80c9a5229650fc77c77559b71552370c35b.svg) Then Cramer's rule states that

$$
x =  \dfrac{D_x}{D}, \qquad y = \dfrac{D_y}{D}
$$

is the unique solution of the system, where
![](images/b1/b13ecd10395fe0977d04d627179667cbca207fcf4015a89d43df0e69765f1f5e.svg)

For example, let's use Cramer's rule to solve the following system of equations:

$$
\{\begin{aligned}3x-2y=-1 \\ -1x+2y=3\end{aligned}
$$

We start by finding the **determinant of the coefficient matrix**:

$$
\begin{aligned}D & =|\begin{aligned}3 & -2 \\ -1 & 2\end{aligned}| \\  & =3\cdot 2-(-1)\cdot (-2) \\  & =4\end{aligned}
$$

Now, we compute $D_x$ and $D_y\mathbin{:}$

$$
\begin{aligned}{D}_{x} & =|\begin{aligned}-1 & -2 \\ 3 & 2\end{aligned}| \\  & =(-1)\cdot 2-3\cdot (-2) \\  & =4 \\ {D}_{y} & =|\begin{aligned}3 & -1 \\ -1 & 3\end{aligned}| \\  & =3\cdot 3-(-1)\cdot (-1) \\  & =8\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, the solution to the system is given by

$$
\begin{aligned}x & =\frac{{D}_{x}}{D}=\frac{4}{4}=1, \\ y & =\frac{{D}_{y}}{D}=\frac{8}{4}=2.\end{aligned}
$$

It is common to write the solutions to a linear system as a vector. So, in this case, we have

$$
\left< x,y \right> = \left< 1,2 \right>.
$$" :db/ensure [:tutorial/validate]} {:db/id 17592186119997 :activity/title "Cramer's Rule for 2x2 Systems of Linear Equations" :activity/expected-seconds 420.0 :db/ensure [:activity/validate]}]

$$
\{\begin{aligned}7x+9y=42 \\ kx+10y=-4.\end{aligned}
$$

Which of the following equations could be solved to find the value of $k?$

I. $|\begin{aligned}7 & 9 \\ k & 10\end{aligned}|=-12$

II. $|\begin{aligned}7 & 9 \\ k & 10\end{aligned}|=-38$

III. $|\begin{aligned}7 & 9 \\ k & 10\end{aligned}|=456$" :question/worked-solution "The determinant of the coefficient matrix is

$$
\begin{aligned}D & =|\begin{aligned}7 & 9 \\ k & 10\end{aligned}|.\end{aligned}
$$

According to Cramer's rule, the value of $x$ is given by $x=\frac{{D}_{x}}{D},$ where

$$
\begin{aligned}{D}_{x} & =|\begin{aligned}42 & 9 \\ -4 & 10\end{aligned}| \\  & =420+36 \\  & =456.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore:

$$
\begin{aligned}x & =\frac{{D}_{x}}{D} \\ -12 & =\frac{456}{|\begin{aligned}7 & 9 \\ k & 10\end{aligned}|} \\ |\begin{aligned}7 & 9 \\ k & 10\end{aligned}| & =\frac{456}{-12} \\ |\begin{aligned}7 & 9 \\ k & 10\end{aligned}| & =-38\end{aligned}
$$

So, the correct answer is "II only"." :question/difficulty :question.difficulty/hard :question/answer-fields ["answer-field-cb7f776c-eb99-528b-aabd-b4033c71b940"] :db/ensure [:question/validate]} {:db/id "answer-field-cb7f776c-eb99-528b-aabd-b4033c71b940" :answer-field/id #uuid "cb7f776c-eb99-528b-aabd-b4033c71b940" :answer-field/key "selection" :answer-field/type :answer-field.type/radio :answer-field/correct "answer-bd29ef89-365b-598b-abba-79648038c1f5" :answer-field/choices ["answer-3cc8305b-aa26-5938-bd09-82bace4ba090" "answer-1f13ed83-8c4f-597b-9f02-b31307021e5b" "answer-f4490cc5-d61d-513b-835c-43fda69e74cc" "answer-bd29ef89-365b-598b-abba-79648038c1f5" "answer-742473cb-daf1-51d3-8173-d6d820c2cd4a"] :db/ensure [:answer-field/validate]} {:db/id "answer-3cc8305b-aa26-5938-bd09-82bace4ba090" :answer/id #uuid "3cc8305b-aa26-5938-bd09-82bace4ba090" :answer/type :answer.type/text :answer/value "I and II only" :db/ensure [:answer/validate]} {:db/id "answer-1f13ed83-8c4f-597b-9f02-b31307021e5b" :answer/id #uuid "1f13ed83-8c4f-597b-9f02-b31307021e5b" :answer/type :answer.type/text :answer/value "I only" :db/ensure [:answer/validate]} {:db/id "answer-f4490cc5-d61d-513b-835c-43fda69e74cc" :answer/id #uuid "f4490cc5-d61d-513b-835c-43fda69e74cc" :answer/type :answer.type/text :answer/value "II and III only" :db/ensure [:answer/validate]} {:db/id "answer-bd29ef89-365b-598b-abba-79648038c1f5" :answer/id #uuid "bd29ef89-365b-598b-abba-79648038c1f5" :answer/type :answer.type/text :answer/value "II only" :db/ensure [:answer/validate]} {:db/id "answer-742473cb-daf1-51d3-8173-d6d820c2cd4a" :answer/id #uuid "742473cb-daf1-51d3-8173-d6d820c2cd4a" :answer/type :answer.type/text :answer/value "III only" :db/ensure [:answer/validate]} {:db/id 17592186121027 :tutorial/content "**Cramer's Rule** is a method for solving a linear system of equations using determinants.

Suppose we have a square system of linear equations

$$
\{\begin{aligned}{a}_{11}x+{a}_{12}y={b}_{1} \\ {a}_{21}x+{a}_{22}y={b}_{2},\end{aligned}
$$

where ![](images/c7/c7ef883a1d4dd8c1fc0fc8fbde5ed80c9a5229650fc77c77559b71552370c35b.svg) Then Cramer's rule states that

$$
x =  \dfrac{D_x}{D}, \qquad y = \dfrac{D_y}{D}
$$

is the unique solution of the system, where
![](images/b1/b13ecd10395fe0977d04d627179667cbca207fcf4015a89d43df0e69765f1f5e.svg)

For example, let's use Cramer's rule to solve the following system of equations:

$$
\{\begin{aligned}3x-2y=-1 \\ -1x+2y=3\end{aligned}
$$

We start by finding the **determinant of the coefficient matrix**:

$$
\begin{aligned}D & =|\begin{aligned}3 & -2 \\ -1 & 2\end{aligned}| \\  & =3\cdot 2-(-1)\cdot (-2) \\  & =4\end{aligned}
$$

Now, we compute $D_x$ and $D_y\mathbin{:}$

$$
\begin{aligned}{D}_{x} & =|\begin{aligned}-1 & -2 \\ 3 & 2\end{aligned}| \\  & =(-1)\cdot 2-3\cdot (-2) \\  & =4 \\ {D}_{y} & =|\begin{aligned}3 & -1 \\ -1 & 3\end{aligned}| \\  & =3\cdot 3-(-1)\cdot (-1) \\  & =8\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, the solution to the system is given by

$$
\begin{aligned}x & =\frac{{D}_{x}}{D}=\frac{4}{4}=1, \\ y & =\frac{{D}_{y}}{D}=\frac{8}{4}=2.\end{aligned}
$$

It is common to write the solutions to a linear system as a vector. So, in this case, we have

$$
\left< x,y \right> = \left< 1,2 \right>.
$$" :db/ensure [:tutorial/validate]} {:db/id 17592186119997 :activity/title "Cramer's Rule for 2x2 Systems of Linear Equations" :activity/expected-seconds 420.0 :db/ensure [:activity/validate]}] "assertions" [[17592186119658 :question/problem "Consider the system of linear equations

"question-9a324339-2131-569e-b62b-73969b420199"] [17592186121027 :tutorial/content "**Cramer's Rule** is a method for solving a linear system of equations using determinants.

Suppose we have a square system of linear equations

$$
\{\begin{aligned}{a}_{11}x+{a}_{12}y={b}_{1} \\ {a}_{21}x+{a}_{22}y={b}_{2},\end{aligned}
$$

where ![](images/c7/c7ef883a1d4dd8c1fc0fc8fbde5ed80c9a5229650fc77c77559b71552370c35b.svg) Then Cramer's rule states that

$$
x =  \dfrac{D_x}{D}, \qquad y = \dfrac{D_y}{D}
$$

is the unique solution of the system, where
![](images/b1/b13ecd10395fe0977d04d627179667cbca207fcf4015a89d43df0e69765f1f5e.svg)

For example, let's use Cramer's rule to solve the following system of equations:

$$
\{\begin{aligned}3x-2y=-1 \\ -1x+2y=3\end{aligned}
$$

We start by finding the **determinant of the coefficient matrix**:

$$
\begin{aligned}D & =|\begin{aligned}3 & -2 \\ -1 & 2\end{aligned}| \\  & =3\cdot 2-(-1)\cdot (-2) \\  & =4\end{aligned}
$$

Now, we compute $D_x$ and $D_y\mathbin{:}$

$$
\begin{aligned}{D}_{x} & =|\begin{aligned}-1 & -2 \\ 3 & 2\end{aligned}| \\  & =(-1)\cdot 2-3\cdot (-2) \\  & =4 \\ {D}_{y} & =|\begin{aligned}3 & -1 \\ -1 & 3\end{aligned}| \\  & =3\cdot 3-(-1)\cdot (-1) \\  & =8\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, the solution to the system is given by

$$
\begin{aligned}x & =\frac{{D}_{x}}{D}=\frac{4}{4}=1, \\ y & =\frac{{D}_{y}}{D}=\frac{8}{4}=2.\end{aligned}
$$

It is common to write the solutions to a linear system as a vector. So, in this case, we have

$$
\left< x,y \right> = \left< 1,2 \right>.

$$
\begin{aligned}D & =|\begin{aligned}3 & -2 \\ -1 & 2\end{aligned}| \\  & =3\cdot 2-(-1)\cdot (-2) \\  & =4\end{aligned}

Express $y$ in terms of $2 \times 2$ determinants." :question/worked-solution "We are given the system

$$
{\begin{aligned}5x+2y=-1 \\ -3x+3y=9.\end{aligned}
$$

The determinant of the coefficient matrix is

$$
\begin{aligned}D & =|\begin{aligned}5 & 2 \\ -3 & 3\end{aligned}|.\end{aligned}
$$

Now, to construct $D_y$, we replace the second column of the coefficient matrix by the right-hand side column of the given system:

$$
\begin{aligned}{D}_{y} & =|\begin{aligned}5 & -1 \\ -3 & 9\end{aligned}|\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, according to Cramer's rule, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}y & =\frac{{D}_{y}}{D}=\frac{|\begin{aligned}5 & -1 \\ -3 & 9\end{aligned}|}{|\begin{aligned}5 & 2 \\ -3 & 3\end{aligned}|}.\end{aligned}
$$"} {:db/id 17592186120437 :question/id #uuid "fe230bdd-3a20-59d7-b749-5cc881ab022a" :question/math-academy-id "q-42605" :knowledge-point/_questions [{:db/id 17592186119788 :knowledge-point/id #uuid "4fcf3704-4856-5095-a6f4-7ec20d81f3c4" :knowledge-point/title "Expressing an Unknown in Terms of 2x2 Determinants"}] :question/answer-fields [{:answer-field/choices [{:answer/id #uuid "948ec8f3-f49e-5c6d-ab2b-f6d15d0c9863" :answer/type {:db/id 17592186045498 :db/ident :answer.type/math} :answer/value "\frac{\begin{vmatrix}2 & -3 \\ 15 & 1\end{vmatrix}}{\begin{vmatrix}1 & -3 \\ 1 & 5\end{vmatrix}}" :db/id 17592186118737} {:answer/id #uuid "9f5af775-d0d7-558d-8f1e-1ecce3b2980c" :answer/type {:db/id 17592186045498 :db/ident :answer.type/math} :answer/value "\frac{\begin{vmatrix}2 & -3 \\ 10 & 5\end{vmatrix}}{\begin{vmatrix}1 & -3 \\ 1 & 5\end{vmatrix}}" :db/id 17592186118738} {:answer/id #uuid "c5a111dd-d69c-5110-8b77-dc40954b19fc" :answer/type {:db/id 17592186045498 :db/ident :answer.type/math} :answer/value "\frac{\begin{vmatrix}2 & -3 \\ 10 & 5\end{vmatrix}}{\begin{vmatrix}-1 & -3 \\ -1 & -5\end{vmatrix}}" :db/id 17592186118739} {:answer/id #uuid "e108a83f-4099-567a-8e94-4cfd178f5fa0" :answer/type {:db/id 17592186045498 :db/ident :answer.type/math} :answer/value "\frac{\begin{vmatrix}1 & -3 \\ 1 & 5\end{vmatrix}}{\begin{vmatrix}1 & -3 \\ 10 & 5\end{vmatrix}}" :db/id 17592186118740} {:answer/id #uuid "ed2fd647-c05e-50f0-a1f2-7416235afe5d" :answer/type {:db/id 17592186045498 :db/ident :answer.type/math} :answer/value "\frac{\begin{vmatrix}3 & -2 \\ 10 & 5\end{vmatrix}}{\begin{vmatrix}1 & -3 \\ 1 & 5\end{vmatrix}}" :db/id 17592186118741}] :answer-field/id #uuid "60a46614-828d-5519-82a8-fe722bf6d03a" :answer-field/key "selection" :answer-field/type {:db/id 17592186045493 :db/ident :answer-field.type/radio} :db/id 17592186118736}] :question/problem "Consider the system of equations

$$
{\begin{aligned}5x-2y=4 \\ x+ky=8\end{aligned}
$$

\begin{aligned}D & =|\begin{aligned}5 & -2 \\ 1 & k\end{aligned}|.\end{aligned}
$$

According to Cramer's rule, the value of $y$ is given by $y=\dfrac{D_y}{D},$ where

$$
\begin{aligned}{D}_{y} & =|\begin{aligned}5 & 4 \\ 1 & 8\end{aligned}| \\  & =5\cdot 8-4\cdot 1 \\  & =36.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore:

$$

"**Cramer's Rule** is a method for solving a linear system of equations using determinants.

Suppose we have a square system of linear equations

$$
{\begin{aligned}{a}_{11}x+{a}_{12}y={b}_{1} \\ {a}_{21}x+{a}_{22}y={b}_{2},\end{aligned}
$$

where $|\begin{aligned}{a}_{11} & {a}_{12} \\ {a}_{21} & {a}_{22}\end{aligned}|$ Then Cramer's rule states that

$$
x =  \dfrac{D_x}{D}, \qquad y = \dfrac{D_y}{D}
$$

is the unique solution of the system, where

$$
|\begin{aligned}{b}_{1} & {a}_{12} \\ {b}_{2} & {a}_{22}\end{aligned}|
$$

For example, let's use Cramer's rule to solve the following system of equations:

$$
{\begin{aligned}3x-2y=-1 \\ -1x+2y=3\end{aligned}
$$

We start by finding the **determinant of the coefficient matrix**:

$$
\begin{aligned}D & =|\begin{aligned}3 & -2 \\ -1 & 2\end{aligned}| \\  & =3\cdot 2-(-1)\cdot (-2) \\  & =4\end{aligned}
$$

Now, we compute $D_x$ and $D_y\mathbin{:}$

$$
\begin{aligned}{D}_{x} & =|\begin{aligned}-1 & -2 \\ 3 & 2\end{aligned}| \\  & =(-1)\cdot 2-3\cdot (-2) \\  & =4 \\ {D}_{y} & =|\begin{aligned}3 & -1 \\ -1 & 3\end{aligned}| \\  & =3\cdot 3-(-1)\cdot (-1) \\  & =8\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, the solution to the system is given by

$$
\begin{aligned}x & =\frac{{D}_{x}}{D}=\frac{4}{4}=1, \\ y & =\frac{{D}_{y}}{D}=\frac{8}{4}=2.\end{aligned}
$$

It is common to write the solutions to a linear system as a vector. So, in this case, we have

$$
\left< x,y \right> = \left< 1,2 \right>.
$$" :tutorial/id #uuid "3adc5c1c-58e5-5c0a-a8f7-da6abd6f06e2" :tutorial/math-academy-id 3102 :tutorial/title "Introduction"} :step/id #uuid "48887938-d6a0-5822-b084-3bf10a3a4461" :step/math-academy-id 16830 :step/next {:db/id 17592186120731}} {:db/id 17592186120731 :step/content {:db/id 17592186119844 :knowledge-point/canonical-example {:db/id 17592186119658 :question/id #uuid "d81e32a1-bd93-5a95-bb4a-e8df9063b5aa" :question/math-academy-id "e-5230"} :knowledge-point/id #uuid "e7580024-f357-57d4-94f2-85c25e2c144b" :knowledge-point/key-prerequisites [{:db/id 17592186049044}] :knowledge-point/questions [{:db/id 17592186120446} {:db/id 17592186120447} {:db/id 17592186271976} {:db/id 17592186329671} {:db/id 17592186329672} {:db/id 17592186338763} {:db/id 17592186338764} {:db/id 17592186392541} {:db/id 17592186402854}] :knowledge-point/title "Identifying the Parts of Cramer's Rule Formula"} :step/id #uuid "720a6f93-380c-5e70-8c81-e99f44a4ef11" :step/math-academy-id 19262 :step/next {:db/id 17592186120647}}] :activity/title "Cramer’s Rule for 2x2 Systems of Linear Equations" :activity/type {:db/id 17592186045463 :db/ident :activity.type/lesson} :db/id 17592186119997} {:db/id 17592186120652 :step/content {:db/id 17592186121027 :tutorial/content "**Cramer's Rule** is a method for solving a linear system of equations using determinants.

17592186045417] [17592186046659 1005 17592186046982 17592186045417] [17592186046659 1007 "Mathematical Methods for the Physical Sciences I" 17592186045417] [17592186046659 1008 "Mathematical Methods for the Physical Sciences I develops the core mathematical structures and analytical tools used throughout theoretical and applied physics. Building on calculus and introductory linear algebra, the course introduces vector geometry, multivariable analysis, and differential equations in a unified framework designed for modeling physical systems.
Students learn how mathematical concepts such as vector spaces, linear transformations, multivariable functions, and differential equations provide the language and computational techniques used to describe motion, fields, and dynamical processes. The course emphasizes connections between abstract mathematical ideas and the physical principles they support, preparing students for advanced study in classical mechanics, electromagnetism, and related areas of physics." 17592186045417] [17592186046659 1009 "The course begins with foundational topics that support later mathematical modeling in physics. Students study vector geometry in three-dimensional space, including equations of lines and planes and geometric relationships between them. These tools appear naturally in the description of trajectories, rays, and intersections of physical surfaces. Introductory set theory provides a precise language for describing mathematical structures and regions in space, supporting later work in multivariable analysis and probability.
Students then develop computational tools from linear algebra. Methods such as Gaussian elimination, matrix inverses, determinants, and LU factorization are used to analyze and solve systems of linear equations. These techniques arise when solving coupled equations in physical models, such as electrical circuits, mechanical systems with multiple interacting components, and discretized approximations of physical fields.
The course next develops the structure of vector spaces and linear transformations. Students study spans, bases, dimension, rank, and null spaces, and extend these ideas to abstract vector spaces. Linear maps and their matrix representations are examined, establishing the connection between geometric transformations and matrix algebra. These ideas culminate in the study of eigenvalues, eigenvectors, and matrix diagonalization, which are central tools for solving differential equations describing oscillations, normal modes of vibration, and stability of dynamical systems.
The course then turns to multivariable calculus and vector analysis. Students analyze functions of several variables, quadric surfaces, and coordinate transformations. Partial derivatives, gradients, and the multivariable chain rule are developed along with linear approximations and higher-order derivatives. These concepts describe how physical quantities such as temperature, pressure, or electric potential vary in space. Vector-valued functions and vector fields are studied together with curvature, divergence, and curl, providing the mathematical language used to describe velocity fields in fluid flow and electric and magnetic fields in electromagnetism.
Students then study multiple integration, focusing on double integrals and coordinate transformations such as polar coordinates. These techniques allow the computation of physical quantities distributed over regions, such as mass, charge, or probability density.
The final portion of the course introduces differential equations as models of dynamical systems. Students study first-order equations and qualitative behavior of solutions through phase-line analysis. Applications include motion under drag, gravitational attraction, electrical circuits, and population dynamics. The course concludes with second-order linear differential equations and oscillatory systems, including harmonic motion, damped oscillators, and resonance—fundamental mathematical models for vibrating
